board.assembly: the panel mounts on the FRONT face, its tail leaves the bottom edge and bends about a HORIZONTAL axis down to board level into J1, which sits below the display band (MECHANICAL_INTERFACE_SPEC item 21, 6 mm bend corridor).  A bend about a horizontal axis PRESERVES left/right; only a route around a board edge and up the rear would mirror it, and no such route is specified.
board.orientation: KiCad's top view IS the F.Cu/front view and +x is to the RIGHT, so J1 pin 1 at x = 44.910 is the RIGHT-hand end of the row and pin 50 at x = 20.410 the LEFT
board.verdict: PIN 1 MEETS PIN 1.  No mirror; J1 is correctly oriented for this panel.

finding.backlight: the same sheet carries the backlight schematic: ONE common LED-A and SIX diodes in parallel, cathodes grouped as LED-K1 (3) and LED-K2 (3) to tail pins 2 and 3, U = 2.9-3.2 V, I = 120 mA.  This independently corroborates D-079, the D-750 true-off analysis and the D-752 open-LED argument.
finding.conclusion: PIN 1 IS AT THE RIGHT-HAND END OF THE TAIL WHEN THE MODULE IS VIEWED FROM ITS DISPLAY FACE WITH THE TAIL AT THE BOTTOM.  The contacts are on the same face as the component/rear side, i.e. they face the PCB.
finding.front_view: section 3.3, the CTP outline drawing: the module FRONT view -- the one labelled 3.5" 320x480 Pixels with the CTP O.D / BL O.D / AA dimension stack -- shows the 50-way tail leaving the BOTTOM edge and labels its ends '50' on the LEFT and '1' on the RIGHT
finding.rear_view: the REAR view on the same sheet, the one carrying the component-area callout and the FPC+PI stiffener dimension 0.3 +/- 0.03 mm, labels '1' on the LEFT and '50' on the RIGHT -- the consistent mirror of the front view, which is what confirms the reading rather than a single ambiguous label

question: external first-spin review item 5: prove the ER-TFT035IPS-6 tail's PHYSICAL pin-1 end, which the FH69's dual-contact feature does NOT settle
residual: the incoming diode-mode test is RETAINED, not because the orientation is still open but because it costs nothing and catches a mis-built tail or a substituted module: the panel's own pins 1/2/3 are LEDA/LEDK/LEDK and 48/49/50 are GND, so a meter reads an LED forward drop of ~2.5-2.9 V between the outermost contact and its two neighbours at the PIN-1 end and a dead short at the other.
